notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: AbstractChannelHandlerContext.isNotValidPromise rejects promise.channel()!=channel()
notApplicableMethods.reason: CLR outbound methods accept EndPoint/message/CancellationToken and return consumer Tasks. Callers cannot submit a mutable producer belonging to another channel; that invalid input is absent from the public API.

notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: isNotValidPromise rejects VoidChannelPromise for close
notApplicableMethods.reason: The CLR API has no VoidChannelPromise argument or void producer object. CloseAsync always returns a normal observable Task; manufacturing this input would add the JVM facade the port deliberately avoids.

notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: isNotValidPromise rejects AbstractChannel.CloseFuture supplied as an operation promise
notApplicableMethods.reason: CloseCompletion is a consumer-only Task with no public setter, and CloseAsync has no completion-producer parameter. A close-notification Task cannot be supplied as a mutable close-operation producer.

notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: validateWrite releases referenceCounted when a wrong-channel promise argument is rejected before transport ownership
notApplicableMethods.reason: The sole rejection trigger in this original helper is channel2.newPromise() supplied to channel1.write. No such parameter exists in CLR WriteAsync. Its exact validation/reference-release scenario is inapplicable, not replaced by an unrelated handler-throw test. Existing native cancellation and rejected-dispatch tests separately cover supported input ownership.

notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: validateWrite releases referenceCounted when wrong-channel promise is supplied to writeAndFlush
notApplicableMethods.reason: WriteAndFlushAsync likewise accepts no completion producer, so a foreign-channel promise cannot enter validation. Do not pretend a generic write failure is the original scenario; supported cancellation/rejection ownership remains separately tested.

notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: ensurePromiseUseCorrectExecutor cascades a context-owned DefaultChannelPromise into a caller-supplied foreign-executor promise; six attached listeners observe context ownership
notApplicableMethods.reason: Native Tasks expose no executor-bearing mutable promise input and do not automatically schedule callbacks on a channel. This exact cascade is absent. A separately counted native test completes all six operations from a foreign producer and explicitly regains the handler owner before observing state; it is a CLR alternative, not the original assertion ported unchanged.

notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: VoidChannelPromise.tryFailure routes a write failure to ExceptionCaught without a returned completion future
notApplicableMethods.reason: Every CLR write returns an observable Task, so there is no explicit VoidChannelPromise failure-notification mode. The native alternative awaits that Task and preserves the original exception identity; it does not manually fire ExceptionCaught to simulate the absent API.

notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: Registration listener initializes OioSocketChannel on a dedicated OioEventLoopGroup
notApplicableMethods.reason: CLR Transport has one asynchronous System.Net.Sockets TcpSocketChannel, not a separate obsolete JVM blocking OIO channel/event-loop family. clrDecisions.subject: Future/Promise/listeners
clrDecisions.decision: Task/TaskCompletionSource and CancellationToken, Task.WhenAll and native delegates. Handler state and completion mutations reenter the explicit executor; native Task continuations do not implicitly inherit event-loop affinity.

clrDecisions.subject: NIO/OIO selector and local IoHandler
clrDecisions.decision: CLR asynchronous Socket operations plus ordered DefaultEventLoop workers; selector classes are not mechanically recreated. Shared observable contracts still require their original tests; unreviewed selector-era contracts remain pending.

clrDecisions.subject: ChannelId
clrDecisions.decision: Guid identity and ordinal text ordering replace the Java MAC/PID/time layout. The Java binary layout is not a wire format; short/long string layout tests remain unreviewed, not marked ported.

clrDecisions.subject: Embedded scheduling resolution
clrDecisions.decision: The public Common scheduling API takes TimeSpan (100 ns ticks). Original EmbeddedChannel testFreezeTime/testCustomTicker use one CLR tick in place of 1 ns; exact-at vs strictly-after deadline checks and all three futures remain.

clrDecisions.subject: Windows UDP truncation
clrDecisions.decision: ReceiveFromAsync does not publish the sender endpoint on WSAEMSGSIZE. Rent 64 KiB while each receive is pending, receive the whole datagram, then truncate to the configured ByteBuf and preserve sender/recipient metadata. This bounds staging per outstanding Windows receive but adds a copy; no platform-performance parity claim.

clrDecisions.subject: FileRegion socket transfer
clrDecisions.decision: Use Socket.SendPacketsAsync with SendPacketsElement(FileStream, long offset, int count) for exact DefaultFileRegion on Windows TCP and Linux TCP/AF_UNIX. .NET dispatches TransmitPackets on Windows and sendfile on Linux. Asynchronous FileStream is required by .NET 10; lazy files use this mode and supplied synchronous streams keep the worker fallback. Preserve opened-handle identity, cursor, 64-bit offsets, bounded ranges, owner progress, and independent native borrow. Custom/derived regions use virtual TransferTo. Unsupported zero-byte submissions can fall back from the recorded offset; partial failed submissions never resend accepted bytes. Kernel tracing establishes native dispatch, not blanket zero-copy/performance equivalence.

clrDecisions.subject: ChannelGroup futures
clrDecisions.decision: Native Task.WhenAll covers currently implemented aggregate operations. Per-channel result/failure inspection remains open; it is not silently excluded as JVM-only.

clrDecisions.subject: Output gathering and cancellation
clrDecisions.decision: Borrowed ReadOnlyMemory arrays and ReadOnlySequence segments replace NIO buffers. Cancellation atomically claims an unflushed Task but retains an empty queue entry until flush; every entry is made consistent before cancelled messages are released or writability callbacks run. TCP sends composite segments; UDP copies segmented content into a single pooled borrow to preserve datagram boundaries.

clrDecisions.subject: Late native I/O completion
clrDecisions.decision: Unlike selector readiness, a CLR receive/accept may already have consumed input when AutoRead or registration is revoked. Keep at most one completed native input operation per channel and dispatch it only after read/registration admission; a close wakes the waiter and releases borrowed memory or the accepted socket. Resume and callback ownership follow the currently registered worker. The source default receive-message limit is 16 for TCP, UDP and server channels; LocalChannel remains 1.

clrDecisions.subject: Pending write producers
clrDecisions.decision: Use native TaskCompletionSource for producer identity/Remove ownership and Task for consumers, Task.WhenAll for aggregation, and CancellationToken for queue/transport cancellation. Queue cancellation retains message ownership until removal and stops at transport flush. Producers are completed on the assigned executor when asynchronous writes finish; Task continuations themselves still require caller-selected dispatch. No Future/Promise/voidPromise facade or JVM Recycler is introduced. The original accounting estimate remains configurable and is not a CLR object-size claim. All source listener reentrance scenarios use default TCS producers and ExecuteSynchronously continuations; consumers await the native bridge when required.

clrDecisions.subject: Coalescing queue completions
clrDecisions.decision: BCL LinkedList stores buffers and native TaskCompletionSource/Action<Task> metadata; no DelegatingChannelPromiseNotifier or Future/Promise/voidPromise facade. Source initial capacity is only a sizing hint, which LinkedList does not use. AddFirst without a producer represents void completion. ReleaseAndFailAll uses Task.FromException and is inherited by CoalescingBufferQueue. WriteAndRemoveAllAsync drains synchronously then exposes native asynchronous write completion with Task.WhenAll. Bridges dispatch notifications to the assigned executor; rejected dispatch fails the native producer and returned Task instead of leaving it pending. Aggregate continuations use ExecuteSynchronously for original inline reentrance; callers selecting asynchronous TCS continuations must await their work. CopyTo intentionally keeps the source shallow-copy ownership contract.

clrDecisions.subject: Native channel pools
clrDecisions.decision: AcquireAsync returns Task<IChannel> and uses CancellationToken; the pool keeps its native TCS producer private. Cancelled consumers still trigger release when pending connect/health checks finish. Async health is Func<IChannel,Task<bool>>, with health invocation and all pool notifications on the channel event loop. BCL LinkedList under a short storage lock replaces a concurrent deque; no user callback runs under that lock. ConcurrentDictionary insertion closes discarded pools outside map operations. Native CloseAsync/DisposeAsync replace GlobalEventExecutor blocking bridges; synchronous Close retains the source blocking caller contract. SimpleChannelPool Close drains available channels and intentionally does not become a permanently closed pool. Bootstrap.Clone(IEventLoop) supplies the source explicit registration owner without making native IEventLoop a fake IEventLoopGroup. JVM stacktrace suppression and mutable Promise overloads are not reproduced.

clrDecisions.subject: Fixed pool ownership and deadlines
clrDecisions.decision: Use a private native TCS per acquisition, CancellationToken for consumer cancellation, TimeSpan for configured durations, a BCL linked pending queue, and ScheduleAsync with a cancellation source per deadline. All count/queue mutations run on one configured event executor. Inner base acquisition remains uncancelled so a cancelled consumer still returns a later successful channel. Base results are explicitly queued back to the pool executor, supplying bounded completion depth when many cancelled requests drain. Handler exceptions return a slot, but ChannelNotAcquiredFromPoolException does not. Native async close replaces the source GlobalEventExecutor blocking bridge and keeps map Get/Remove nonblocking across workers. Monotonic executor ticker and unchecked deadline subtraction preserve wrap-safe expiry; duration conversion saturates rather than overflows. JVM fillInStackTrace suppression is omitted while preserving its comment and native stacks.

clrDecisions.subject: Local segmented reads and original read budgets
clrDecisions.decision: Use the existing indexed ByteBuf.WriteBytes overload for coalescing, exactly as upstream: a live CLR ReadOnlyMemory can describe only contiguous storage, so treating every ByteBuf as one memory is invalid. Indexed transfer supports every segment and preserves source reader indices. Restore the source nonempty-inbound condition before consuming a pending read, so a late empty peer notification cannot lose the next manual Read. Original concurrency/read count inputs and 5-second deadlines stay unchanged; native async test signals replace blocking latches and Task continuations explicitly regain executor ownership before Read. The package-visible inbound queue is exposed to the original friend-assembly test by an internal read-only empty-state property, without exposing a mutable public collection.

clrDecisions.subject: Local lifecycle, native connect completion and close-owned writes
clrDecisions.decision: Keep native Task/TCS producers, consumer cancellation and explicit owner dispatch. Complete the on-owner connect operation before ChannelActive while retaining asynchronous continuation scheduling. SocketException(ConnectionRefused) represents failed remote acceptance and IOException represents own/closed-channel failure. Never touch a pending accepted peer owned by a server or registration loop. Finish peer reads using the source writeInProgress ordering. A short CLR inbound acceptance gate joins publication with close/seal, with no user retain/release callbacks under it. Preserve original write/close test assertions; use deterministic CLR supplements for inline write finalization reentrance and retained-reference handoff races. CLR pending-connect cancellation cancels the private producer and closes on its owner; later server acceptance cannot reactivate the client. A delayed separate-executor initializer must still receive Registered/read/removal after close; pending-context admission happens before executor dispatch and invocation-state filtering after it. Source volatile link/state visibility is retained.

clrDecisions.subject: Pipeline mutations and optional concurrent removal
clrDecisions.decision: Port the three original lookup forms using C# string, IChannelHandler and Type. A shared TryRemoveContext atomically unlinks under the existing pipeline gate, defers removal until first registration or queues it on the assigned owner, and returns false for a lost unlink race. Optional removal returns null; normal removal throws KeyNotFoundException. Preserve buffered forwarding through removed/replaced contexts and unresolved source write completions. Native Task/TCS and BCL queue/channel helpers retain the original callback counts and executor order without reproducing a Java Promise API.

clrDecisions.subject: Pipeline pending admission and primary initialization failure
clrDecisions.decision: Use the existing IOrderedEventExecutor marker and private CLR volatile/Interlocked state to preserve source ADD_PENDING admission without recreating Java field-updater APIs. An unordered executor can deliver an event before queued HandlerAdded starts; a normal event loop cannot. Added state is committed before reentrant user callbacks, and removal is finalized even if a callback throws. Added-failure cleanup logs secondary removal errors while preserving the primary pipeline exception. Pre-cancelled tokens replace supplied cancelled promises; native cancellation/dispatch Tasks are explicitly observed before inspecting completion and buffer ownership. Recheck admission when routing a callback failure because that callback may already have removed its own context. The original DefaultEventLoop-based alternating helper retains the existing native ordered marker.

clrDecisions.subject: Pipeline mask, method-level decisions and native completion roles
clrDecisions.decision: Preserve meaningful @Skip behavior using a non-inherited CLR method attribute, concrete interface-map targets and an immutable weak-key cache. Skip event-specific forwarding only on the same executor; crossing a foreign executor remains necessary for order. Do not reintroduce caller-owned Java promises, void promises, mutable close futures or a duplicate blocking OIO backend merely to compile invalid-input tests. Explicitly reviewed unsupported source methods remain separate from mapped source cases and native supplements. Task consumers must explicitly dispatch owner state access; their returned failure Task preserves exception identity.

clrDecisions.subject: Combined handler contexts and native completion plumbing
clrDecisions.decision: Keep ChannelHandlerContext as the existing concrete public type and permit internal delegation by virtualizing IsRemoved and its forwarding operations. Both owned contexts delegate to the current outer context and expose the outer Handler identity exactly as source; removal flags and callbacks remain independent. Returned Tasks preserve the positive completion intent of testPromisesPassed, while source-specific invalid mutable-input tests remain distinct. Six additional native tests verify facade identity, live neighbors, foreign-thread removal, lifecycle failure/finally, removal failure and controlled Task outcomes.

clrDecisions.subject: Datagram multicast TTL option
clrDecisions.decision: DefaultDatagramChannelConfig.getTimeToLive/setTimeToLive and the NIO IP_MULTICAST_TTL option concern multicast, not Socket.Ttl. Use SocketOptionName.MulticastTimeToLive at the socket family IP/IPv6 level with 0..255 validation. Two supplemental CLR cases independently read the actual socket option, preserve unicast TTL, round-trip 0/17/255 and reject -1/256/int.MaxValue. Both fail against the former unicast mapping. Multicast interface/address options and membership fixtures remain open.

clrDecisions.subject: UDP testsuite, multicast selection and connected lifecycle
clrDecisions.decision: Track selected testsuite originals separately from the exhaustive 274-file Transport inventory. Preserve both pooled/adaptive allocators, IPv4/IPv6 families, all buffer representations/wraps and original helper assertions. Config options reflect actual socket state. Track ASM memberships with BCL tuple keys to preserve repeated join/leave behavior. The inherited IPv6 multicast fixture retains its Windows assumption and executes with both allocators on Linux. Use the documented Winsock zero-address UDP connect to disconnect without replacing its bound socket; retain channel peer state separately from Socket cached connection state. Datagram individual write failures do not close a channel that may send to another peer; unresolved endpoints fail before native send and release ownership. Registered-only activity defers CLR receive until a first send implicitly binds the socket. The public DatagramChannelConfig disabled-loopback contract and DefaultDatagramChannelConfig behavior are retained using !Socket.MulticastLoopback. NioDatagramChannelConfig forwards IP_MULTICAST_LOOP directly despite that disabled-name contract; native tests independently verify actual kernel loopback state, not just getter/setter symmetry.

clrDecisions.subject: Source-specific multicast, read failures and resolver cancellation
clrDecisions.decision: IPv4 source inclusion/drop and all-source blocking use BCL SocketOptionName with platform-reviewed IP_MREQ_SOURCE byte layout (Windows group/source/interface; Linux group/interface/source). Tuple keys distinguish source memberships, reject ASM/SSM mixing and retain idempotence. Blocking a missing membership is a no-op; implicit block uses the selected native multicast interface consistently with implicit join instead of the original bound-wildcard lookup pitfall. IPv6 source filtering uses the native group_source_req ABI on Windows and Linux via Socket.SetRawSocketOption. Its interface index identifies the IPv6 zone, so scoped and unscoped forms share the same membership key. The ABI for other operating systems remains open. Socket read failures emit ReadComplete then ExceptionCaught and preserve outstanding manual read permission; other read errors close. Connect cancellation races an independent resolver Task and closes promptly even if the resolver ignores its token; observe late failures without changing the canceled result or retaining the channel.

clrDecisions.subject: Initializer extension discovery and ordered typed bootstrap state
clrDecisions.decision: Use explicit scoped process-wide Register rather than inventing a Java SPI/Classpath loader in CLR. Default registry is empty; opt-in/log-only mode, source floating-point priority order, immutable captures and exception isolation preserve actual policy. Client/listener callbacks run during pre-registration initialization; child callback runs after child options/attributes/handler setup and before registration. Notifications retain source role/thread-local semantics. OrderedDictionary preserves option insertion order; typed-key dictionaries retain attribute values/actions, replace updates and remove nulls without materializing an empty channel attribute. Both client and server clone/capture state independently. Preserve Java LinkedHashMap plus synchronized snapshots using OrderedDictionary guarded by a private lock, and ConcurrentHashMap attributes using ConcurrentDictionary of typed keys/value-application pairs. Caller mutation cannot corrupt option snapshots; clone option order remains independent. Other builder-wide concurrency remains unreviewed.

clrDecisions.subject: Bootstrap configuration views and failure/completion representation
clrDecisions.decision: Use native get-only live Config views and independent ReadOnlyDictionary snapshots backed by ordered BCL maps. Remove Java self-typed generic bootstrap plumbing; resolver metadata is object identity while actual resolution remains typed, atomically paired in an immutable record. Null resolver resets the default. Retain source volatile visibility. Task consumers explicitly return to the event loop for owner callbacks; Tasks do not inherit Java ChannelFuture listener affinity. The original factory-failure method requires a dummy FailedChannel result carrier, so it is reviewed as CLR-inapplicable in full and has a separately counted native Task-fault alternative. Preserve its completion deadline and exception identity without fabricating a channel.

clrDecisions.subject: TCP direction shutdown, allocator-owned manual read batches and final input-read notification
clrDecisions.decision: Use Task-based direction shutdown, output before input, always attempt both and preserve the original output exception via ExceptionDispatchInfo. IOException replaces closed-channel representation; the dedicated ChannelOutputShutdownException subtype preserves queued-write failure meaning. Output shutdown fails/releases queued ownership and emits its event even when the native call fails, retaining input registration and communication. One explicit Read admits the whole allocator-approved available batch; a held first native completion still respects disabled AutoRead and deregistration. CLR has no later readiness callback after EOF, so the next admitted logical read emits the final ReadComplete/InputShutdownReadComplete pair once on the current owner. Source tests keep original data sizes, allocator budgets, boolean combinations, direction roles, ownership and deadlines. No selector, Java future facade or copied comment archive is introduced.

clrDecisions.subject: TCP write-error classification and half-close backend/platform conditions
clrDecisions.decision: Java SocketException inherits IOException; CLR SocketException does not. Treat both as I/O errors for AutoClose=true; otherwise shut output only, wrap the original cause, release queued references and keep input usable. Close transport before faulting flushed tasks; keep separate unflushed closed causes. SO_LINGER=0 must skip orderly Socket.Shutdown so Dispose sends an abortive reset. Preserve the original Windows assumption instead of forcing Unix reset/read ordering onto Windows. The kernel-specific no-manual-read half-close scenario is explicitly excluded just as the original excludes NIO/OIO; the CLR backend counterpart requests reads and stays supplementary. Preserve the original incorrect Context-cast scenario as its actual exception/peer-close path and separately test a real half-close. All eight SocketHalfClosed declarations are accounted without rewriting assertions or counting gated/no-op wrapper calls as passed test bodies.

clrDecisions.subject: Event-loop native scheduling, registration result roles and polymorphic queue metrics
clrDecisions.decision: Java virtual instance dispatch must remain virtual in CLR: replace the hidden new PendingTasks member by a true override, with a source-shaped held-owner test proving ordinary plus tail counts through the parent type. Native Task/CTS retain scheduling deadlines, non-overlap and cancellation while avoiding Java scheduled futures/promises. DelayNanos expects the source absolute clock input, so native helper adds the ticker initial offset to elapsed nanoseconds before conversion. A caller-supplied channel promise that completes but cannot dispatch its listener through a stopped owner has no native producer-input equivalent; it stays explicitly CLR-inapplicable, while native Task consumer notification is separately verified. Four deregistration enum forms fold to the two native context/channel routes; owner dispatch is explicit before and after moving the real channel. Original comments/assertions/timing bounds, tail removal/drain and cleanup count remain intact.

clrDecisions.subject: Native I/O registration, server accept batching and wakeup semantics
clrDecisions.decision: Track actual owned channel registrations in the production CLR loop, expose owner-only read-only snapshots and feed registration counts into suspension admission. Register/deregister/migrate/close/forced-failure paths maintain membership. A BCL listening Socket is owned directly by native listener/stream constructors. Reuse the existing source server allocator (message count, ignore bytes) rather than the stream adaptive allocator; collect an available accept batch before callbacks, deliver partial accepts before completion/error, preserve manual read permission on empty recoverable failures and consume it when messages were delivered. IOException/CLR SocketException are recoverable, other accept failures close; yield after synchronous failures. Java selector rebuilding/identity/interest masks and NioChannelOption adapter roles are explicitly excluded in full, not represented by dummy CLR types. Source B/C loop helpers now use AutoResetEvent to wake a wait: Thread.Interrupt is not a safe CLR translation of Java wakeup, because CLR can interrupt Monitor lock acquisition during callback logging. Real source timing/ownership assertions remain unchanged. Completed native write operations release their temporary borrow before publishing a queued failure, matching source release-before-notification while retaining any still-running native operation borrow during close.

clrDecisions.subject: Unix domain stream and listener channels
clrDecisions.decision: Share native asynchronous read, write, connect and accept behavior with TCP. Use BCL AF_UNIX endpoints and sockets, preserve role-specific receive/send/backlog/half-close options and let BCL socket disposal clean up paths it bound. Capability checks replace the JDK version gate. The JDK unsupported-option and three VoidPromise identity fixtures are reviewed as complete methods. A test-only wakeup signal is serialized with disposal to keep the original event-loop assertions runnable.

clrDecisions.subject: Transport group scaling and worker suspension
clrDecisions.decision: The existing group can opt into Common chooser policies. Managed async socket completions and local channel callbacks use the same owner queue, so dispatch time feeds utilization and blocking queue time stays idle. Real channel registrations guard both suspension request and owner transition. Direct work can resume a cached loop without chooser selection, so the monitor reconciles newly active capacity while preserving published scale-ups whose workers are still starting. Wakeup enqueue and terminal state publication are serialized to avoid late sentinels after final drain.

clrDecisions.subject: Caller-owned manual I/O event loop
clrDecisions.decision: Reuse the native scheduled-work queue and physical executor mapping. Use one owner thread, Monitor wakeups, the configured ticker for deadlines, and real managed channel registration for shutdown ownership. Expose the loop through IEventLoopGroup so both bootstraps can use it directly. There is no separate Java selector handler phase in this managed pump. Synchronous Java bulk invocation has no CLR producer API.

clrDecisions.subject: Manual managed inbound socket phase
clrDecisions.decision: Drive managed socket accept and receive completions before regular callbacks. I/O-only and task-only pumps have separate queues. Count distinct channels whose inbound completions were delivered, excluding wakeups, timers, rearming and closed or moved completions. Bound the snapshot and follow the current registered owner before dispatch. Drain accepted callbacks during shutdown so their work can settle and buffers can be released. Queued completions retain submission ExecutionContext while the physical executor mapping stays on the owner.

clrDecisions.subject: Socket connect and outbound completion dispatch
clrDecisions.decision: Reject a second connect while the first is pending, and reject a new stream connect once active without closing the first connection. Route pending managed socket send and connect results through the manual I/O phase. Control callbacks and synchronous operations do not increase the count. Retain the primary failure and the outbound buffer borrow until the native operation has returned. A cancellation after native connect but before owner publication still emits ChannelActive, then closes, preserving the source order. The original timeout and cancellation fixtures use a controllable pending primitive in CLR and keep the source time bounds.

clrDecisions.subject: Stream socket gathering writes
clrDecisions.decision: Use the managed Socket.SendAsync array-vector overload for at most sixteen compatible memory segments, bounded by the adaptive send window. The vector is a prefix of flushed byte buffers. Borrow each covered buffer until the native operation completes, then commit exactly the returned bytes using ChannelOutboundBuffer.RemoveBytes. Direct-memory segments, file regions and custom stream write overrides retain their own path. Write-spin yielding and asynchronous rearm resume only the existing flush. Retain all six source methods and both allocator modes; the JVM heap-dump TODO is tracked separately.

clrDecisions.subject: UDP receive batches and IPv4-mapped traffic
clrDecisions.decision: Use the original allocator continue-reading rule with a native readiness hint, including short UDP datagrams. Deliver each received message once, complete the batch once, then publish any error. Recoverable SocketException preserves an empty manual-read request. A not-yet-complete follow-up receive may be carried into the next batch with its buffer still borrowed. DualMode is explicit on IPv6 sockets; derived mapped fixtures use an IPv4 wildcard bind and IPv4 loopback destination. Keep all eleven inherited methods and both original allocators without counting inherited declarations twice.

clrDecisions.subject: Linux IPv6 traffic class
clrDecisions.decision: The Java IP_TOS contract maps to the IPv6 socket traffic class. The CLR TypeOfService option at the IPv6 level returns OperationNotSupported on Linux. Use the Linux IPV6_TCLASS option with native-endian int payloads. Other socket families and platforms retain their existing BCL path.

clrDecisions.subject: Linux UDP peer detach
clrDecisions.decision: Use Linux connect(AF_UNSPEC) on the existing descriptor. Restore the original binding when the kernel releases its port. Read the native endpoint on state changes because Socket.LocalEndPoint caches connected endpoints. Preserve pending receives and socket options. Close if the original binding cannot be restored after detaching the peer.

clrDecisions.subject: Linux multicast membership isolation and mapped IPv4
clrDecisions.decision: Disable IP_MULTICAST_ALL and IPV6_MULTICAST_ALL at supported native levels as OpenJDK does. Select the membership level by group family, including IPv4 on a Linux dual-mode socket. Set the IPv4 interface, multicast hops, loopback and traffic class alongside the IPv6 options where applicable. Preserve live kernel memberships when disconnecting. Native connect SocketException closes the channel as in NioDatagramChannel.

clrDecisions.subject: Reentrant writes and queued writability
clrDecisions.decision: Charge queued writes before submission and release the reservation before handler dispatch or when submission fails. The owner publishes deferred writability changes for task bytes and immediate changes for buffer entries. A queued write-and-flush resolves the combined handler mask and calls both operations in one executor callback. Task cancellation and fault paths release the queued message once.

clrDecisions.subject: Local transport connection failure cleanup and thread model
clrDecisions.decision: Close a registered LocalChannel when its connect-time local bind or peer lookup fails. Preserve the original error and release its address so it can be bound again. Thread-model fixtures retain original thread affinity, lifecycle order, counts and deadlines. The six source-disabled methods are compiled, recorded separately and skipped.

clrDecisions.subject: Threaded socket completion phases and I/O ratio
clrDecisions.decision: Both loops share completion capture and Task transfer. The threaded owner drains a snapshot before ordinary work. Only callbacks reporting handled I/O contribute to the proportional budget. Administrative phases use the source maximum. The source default is 100 and invalid values outside 1..100 are rejected. Idle iterations retain existing task-only scheduling. UDP preparation and admission may span separate turns. Public raw registrations and backend identity are open.

clrDecisions.subject: Standalone completion registrations and backend queries
clrDecisions.decision: Use existing CLR async operations and publish their results to the registration. The callback runs on the loop owner, manual counting groups results by registration, and cancellation completes after the owner unregisters without disposing. Shutdown disposes remaining valid handles. Backend factories are per worker and compatibility and exact-type queries do not consume the chooser.

clrDecisions.subject: Prepare and deliver ready UDP batches in one I/O phase
clrDecisions.decision: Wait for CLR receive completion without consuming its result, then apply allocator accounting and deliver the ready batch on the owner in the same I/O callback. Keep unfinished follow-up receives for the next admitted cycle. UDP errors with no delivered packets remain uncounted.

clrDecisions.subject: Segmented UDP writes and Linux receive offload
clrDecisions.decision: Use per-message UDP_SEGMENT on eligible Linux sockets and separate datagrams on the managed fallback. Enable UDP_GRO and scattering slot size before registration so an outstanding managed receive cannot consume control metadata. The Linux path uses non-blocking recvmsg or recvmmsg and CLR async peek for readiness. Retained slices preserve individual datagram lengths and sender addresses after the aggregate buffer is released.

clrDecisions.subject: Linux UDP original destination and nonlocal bind
clrDecisions.decision: Parse IPv4 original destination and UDP_GRO control messages together for both recvmsg and recvmmsg. Propagate the per-packet recipient to retained segments and use the channel local endpoint when ancillary metadata is absent. Configure original destination before registration so a pending CLR read cannot consume it. Map IP_FREEBIND to the native Linux socket flag.

clrDecisions.subject: Linux listener and TCP stream socket options
clrDecisions.decision: Use native Linux socket option values for port sharing, listener free bind, defer-accept, cork, quick-ACK and the full unsigned NOTSENT_LOWAT range. Apply the configured Fast Open queue before listen. Keep Linux-only options scoped to their matching socket and channel type.

clrDecisions.subject: Linux TCP MD5 authentication and address-only binding
clrDecisions.decision: Use the native TCP_MD5SIG ABI with write-only keys. Validate the complete replacement before mutation, serialize kernel updates, track only successful peer changes and clear temporary key bytes. Unsupported authentication options fail channel initialization. The channel refreshes a cached port-zero endpoint from getsockname after connect.

clrDecisions.subject: Client Fast Open and queued initial data
clrDecisions.decision: Enable Linux TCP_FASTOPEN_CONNECT when a flushed initial ByteBuf is available. Use managed ConnectAsync and the first SendAsync so the CLR tracks socket state and cancellation. Bound the initial prefix to the kernel TCP_MAXSEG and remove only accepted bytes on the owner. Retain its buffer until native completion. Empty queues and unsupported platforms use ordinary connect. Separate managed connect and send avoid the .NET 10 pending ConnectAsync-with-buffer failure path that suppressed completion callbacks in the isolated diagnostic.

clrDecisions.subject: Core channel errors and channel-group Task failures
clrDecisions.decision: Preserve closed-channel failure causes through IOException.InnerException and use SocketException(NotConnected) for open inactive channels. Close on Java-style I/O failures before releasing queued ownership. Keep Tasks as the awaitable aggregate; ChannelGroupException is a CLR AggregateException that enumerates immutable channel/cause pairs. Child cancellation is a correlated group failure, and a child AggregateException retains every inner cause.

clrDecisions.subject: Shared output shutdown and full-close default
clrDecisions.decision: AbstractChannel owns output admission, queue causes and the shutdown event. Socket streams override only the native shutdown primitive. Default shutdown uses ordinary CLR close/lifecycle cleanup because open/active/registration state is held by AbstractChannel. Queue admission closes before native work, while references and completion are released afterward. Native I/O exception classes retain the source AutoClose policy; datagrams retain their continue-per-message exception behavior.

clrDecisions.subject: Native per-channel group operation observation
clrDecisions.decision: Async methods return a native aggregate Task and optionally an out IReadOnlyDictionary<IChannel, Task>. The immutable snapshot supplies lookup and Values iteration; standard Task status queries supply source partial completion. Successful = IsCompletedSuccessfully; failed = IsCompleted && !IsCompletedSuccessfully, including cancellation. The group is the receiver. There is no new Future/Promise wrapper or public producer. WaitAsync cancellation withdraws the observer; it does not cancel children. JVM listener removal and the blocking deadlock hook are adapted to the native async-observer model; Task.Wait itself has no JVM guard. RemoveById avoids making existing Remove(null) ambiguous.

clrDecisions.subject: Manual read before activation and decoder test adaptation
clrDecisions.decision: Completion-based sockets cannot issue a receive before connect. Retain that read permission until activation, consume it through the existing owner read path and clear it with read-pending state. The not-yet-connected fixture uses a four-byte native test collector with the source ByteToMessageDecoder manual continuation for fragmented input; no codec implementation is claimed.

clrDecisions.subject: Logical file-region completion and CLR producer ownership
clrDecisions.decision: Use region.Transferred() as both transfer position and the completion predicate. A framed region may logically consume more source bytes than it writes to the target. Keep the synchronous Stream producer serialized off the event-loop worker and commit actual returned progress on the owner. The queue and active producer hold independent reference ownership; channel closure can fail a queued Task while the native worker keeps its borrow until it exits. The supplemental close-during-producer test records this CLR-specific lifetime separately from original fixture mappings.

clrDecisions.subject: FileRegion Stream target on nonblocking owned sockets
clrDecisions.decision: NetworkStream rejects nonblocking sockets. The internal Stream target preserves socket mode, loops over partial Socket.Send results, waits on Poll write readiness only on the offloaded file worker, retains IOException/inner SocketException failure structure and never owns/disposes the channel socket. Real nonblocking full-data and close-during-long-transfer cases verify backpressure and final producer release on Windows and Linux.

clrDecisions.subject: SocketFileRegion VoidPromise test adaptation
clrDecisions.decision: The two original VoidPromise tests still execute their complete mixed ByteBuf/empty-region/file-region success bodies, including manual-read variation and full wire data. C# Task observation is intentionally ignored in these cases; no meaningless caller-supplied promise singleton or identity comparison is added. Observable write completions and reference release are checked in the other file and buffer-lifetime cases. This does not claim an exact JVM VoidPromise API or its error-listener representation.

clrDecisions.subject: Windows AF_UNIX overlapped EOF completion
clrDecisions.decision: On Windows NT 10.0.26300 with .NET 10.0.7, the original 100-connection domain fixture intermittently leaves one server ReceiveAsync pending after all clients close. A standalone BCL-only echo probe also reproduces it: Poll(SelectRead)=true, Available=0, synchronous Peek=0, while the already posted async receive stays incomplete. Shutdown(Send) and DisconnectAsync alternatives also reproduce the hang; no close-only workaround is retained. Only Windows AF_UNIX uses a single-reader readiness-gated synchronous receive on an asynchronous worker, with 1/2/4/8/10 ms polling backoff. No idle connection pins a blocked worker and no receive blocks the event loop. Delivery, reference ownership, read admission and native socket mode remain unchanged. Polling adds timer/allocation/idle CPU cost and readiness latency; no Windows AF_UNIX performance parity is claimed. The exact OS versus runtime defect and applicability to other Windows/runtime versions are not established.

clrDecisions.subject: Real connection-attempt originals versus deterministic CLR timing tests
clrDecisions.decision: The original timeout/cancellation bodies again use actual socket connects and the source network-route prerequisite. Preserve the configurable bad host/port and original observation windows; the timeout original checks completion, not an invented timeout-only assertion. Keep held-native-connect timing checks in SocketConnectTimingContractTest as four supplemental cases. These no longer count as replacements for real source executions. Native cancellation tokens replace future.cancel, and refused/half-closure scenarios continue to verify real refusal and no ChannelActive.

clrDecisions.subject: Channel transport progress in the CLR
clrDecisions.decision: ChannelConfig.WriteProgress is an optional IProgress<ChannelWriteProgress> captured at native outbound queue admission. Reports contain the channel, the actual queue Task and immutable TransferProgress, without a borrowed message reference or a public completion producer. Counts/totals follow ChannelOutboundBuffer.total/progress for ByteBuf, FileRegion, ByteBufHolder and unknown messages. The observer is opt-in per configuration snapshot; later configuration changes do not alter queued writes. Existing outbound handler signatures stay intact. Progress is called by the owner before its queue Task completes; the IProgress implementation controls actual callback dispatch. A standard Progress<T> may dispatch later, while Common ExecutorProgress gives explicit ordered progress/terminal notifications and removable observation. Direct Report exceptions are logged and isolated from I/O. Outer pipeline/executor Tasks may differ from the reported transport Task, especially after encoding/splitting. No source progress is synthesized from completion, no exact public JVM promise identity API is claimed, and invalid source ranges are not delivered.

clrDecisions.subject: Native channel-group collection and comparison surface
clrDecisions.decision: Use ISet<IChannel>, IComparable<DefaultChannelGroup> and standard reference-based HashSet algorithms. Union/symmetric difference admit through Add so stayClosed and close observation remain intact; removal/intersection do not close channels. Identity equality/hash remain independent of membership, name comparison is ordinal and same-name ties use RuntimeHelpers identity hashes. CLR null comparison follows the BCL convention. ToArray gives a server-first, non-null, independent membership snapshot. CopyTo follows native array argument/capacity rules; no transaction across concurrent separate calls is promised. As with other concurrent ICollection implementations, prefer the concrete snapshot ToArray when concurrent membership changes matter; arbitrary external Count-plus-CopyTo/LINQ optimizations are not an atomic operation. ChannelIds have the original uniqueness precondition. Func predicates, Boolean composition and ordinary enumeration replace ChannelMatcher/CombinedIterator facades.

clrDecisions.subject: TCP configuration roles and JDK versus CLR socket option semantics
clrDecisions.decision: Keep the existing typed ChannelOption API and shared DefaultSocketChannelConfig, with separate TCP listener/stream and domain option sets; no fluent Java config hierarchy is recreated. Unsupported options return false and do not touch the native socket. Listener backlog uses the platform SOMAXCONN equivalent with Volatile access. JDK Socket rejects nonpositive receive/send sizes and limits enabled linger to 65535 seconds, while negative linger disables it; enforce those semantics before passing CLR socket options. Initialize TCP_NODELAY once, best effort, when constructing the native channel so lazy Config creation cannot overwrite later caller/accepted-socket choices. Linux IPv6 uses raw IPV6_TCLASS, also setting IPv4 TOS for dual-mode peers. Traffic-class input must be 0..255. Native get returns actual OS policy rather than a fabricated cached echo. Java performance preferences have no CLR counterpart and are not represented by a no-op API. Non-Linux IPv6 traffic-class policy and wider subinterface source comments are not claimed complete.

clrDecisions.subject: Message write quanta and empty UDP buffers
clrDecisions.decision: Use a nullable write-message limit hook in the shared native drain: UDP snapshots DefaultChannelConfig.GetMaxMessagesPerWrite or the public option on custom configs, falling back to int.MaxValue when absent. Other transports retain their own policies. Each removed message, including a recoverable failure or cancelled empty placeholder, consumes one slot. Re-arm a native I/O continuation at quantum expiry, with next-phase snapshots and ordinary-task opportunity; no selector or promise facade is introduced. A resumed drain owns the same exclusive writer claim, including pending native borrows, close and reentrant flush. Do not send zero-length buffers: the original NIO message writer completes them before checking a peer. Native empty receive behavior remains intact. Read the optional active-on-registration setting through IChannelConfig instead of casting custom configs to a private type. The old supplemental zero-send expectation was inconsistent with the original and is corrected to assert that a following marker is the first/only received datagram; original JUnit mappings/assertions are unchanged.

clrDecisions.subject: Scalar ByteBuf write quantum and source identifiers
clrDecisions.decision: Port DoWrite0/DoWriteInternal/DoWriteBytes with the original names and mapped variables, using Task results for CLR native producers. Commit ByteBuf state on the event-loop owner and keep an independent native borrow until completion. Successful nonempty scalar/vector OS writes each consume one shared spin; empty entries consume zero. Config is read once per pass. Asynchronous CLR sends already wait for readiness, so an invalid completed nonempty result fails rather than creating a fake selector operation. Preserve custom whole-message DoWrite overrides and expose the source-named DoWriteBytes producer in the existing fallback too. The protected DoWriteAsync contract is renamed DoWrite throughout Transport implementations/tests; the earlier CLR message-limit hook is now MaxMessagesPerWrite. Preserve original method/variable names going forward, with only requested capitalization/underscore changes. File-region quantum behavior is recorded separately; broader custom whole-message eligibility remains under review.

clrDecisions.subject: Per-attempt file-region production and zero-progress retry
clrDecisions.decision: Keep DoWriteFileRegion, region, position, localFlushedAmount and WRITE_STATUS_SNDBUF_FULL source identifiers. The native-capable write loop retains a file producer through one attempt, charges zero for already-complete regions and one for accepted positive bytes, and retries a zero result on a later write turn using the original full-buffer status. Do not infer logical completion from physical byte count. The native default-file producer sends one bounded range and commits its accepted counter on the owner; custom/synchronous producers invoke TransferTo once on a worker. Preserve partial-error progress, opened-handle identity, long offsets, async-file constraints, safe capability fallback and independent producer borrows through close. The older supplemental zero-progress failure expectation is corrected from direct original-implementation evidence; no original JUnit assertion changes. Custom whole-message opt-out eligibility remains a separate adaptation to review.

clrDecisions.subject: Adaptive socket gathering limits and source identifiers
clrDecisions.decision: Keep AdjustMaxBytesPerGatheringWrite(attempted, written, oldMaxBytesPerGatheringWrite), CalculateMaxBytesPerGatheringWrite/newSendBufferSize and Get/SetMaxBytesPerGatheringWrite names. Snapshot the window for scalar and vector sends; account actual attempted segment bytes and preserve Java overflowing signed-int doubling rather than saturating to int.MaxValue. Include the first ByteBuf whole even above maxBytes, then stop before a later message would exceed the hint. Keep the existing portable sixteen-segment CLR vector cap and native producer borrows. Compare/exchange prevents stale async production from replacing a newer explicit send-buffer configuration. NioBuffers still returns borrowed reusable ReadOnlyMemory<byte> views, with source-named NioBufferCount/NioBufferSize properties and ClearNioBuffers. No JVM buffer facade is introduced. Six existing original buffer-view tests keep their names, source variables and original assertions. This is a scoped identifier audit; historical counterparts elsewhere remain open.

clrDecisions.subject: Positive-linger native close and shutdown-owned completion
clrDecisions.decision: PrepareToClose returns TaskScheduler.Default for an open native TCP socket with positive linger; disabled/zero/disposed sockets retain owner close. DoClose0 performs native disposal; duplicate closes join closeFuture. Quiesce CLR logical open/active/queue admission first in place of selector-key cancellation, then fail queued writes and fire inactive/unregistered/removal on the owner after native close. Keep the existing CLR CloseCompletion boundary after owner cleanup. Reserve completion admission independently of public task rejection, and hold loop termination/actual suspension until the reserved callback drains. Manual shutdown starts close without synchronously waiting on its own owner. A CLR scheduler rejection closes synchronously and releases its reservation; an already-running close keeps disposal ownership even if CloseForcibly is requested. Runtime close failure reaches the first Task; repeated close/CloseCompletion still succeed after cleanup. Native write borrows survive queue release until producer completion. Source methods/variables/comments remain at reviewed counterparts; ReserveCloseCompletion and its queues are explicitly CLR-only admission plumbing. Original SocketRstTest retains its default setup and stronger native ConnectionReset check without an IOException wrapper.

openWork.detail: TCP receive, TCP accept and UDP receive now withhold a completed native operation after AutoRead=false; read resumes without dropping input. Deregistered TCP input waits for registration and moves to the new worker. Native integration tests also cover buffer/socket cleanup while paused. Remaining: further registration/rejection and half-closure variants, complete read-batch budgets, and original socket/IoHandler fixture review. Native accept batching now uses the original server message allocator and proves 2/1 grouping, partial-batch error ordering, empty-failure manual permission retention and fatal closure. closedInboundOwnership.sourceMeaning: A successful local write does not promise remote delivery, but every accepted or rejected retained reference must have a single release owner. BCL ConcurrentQueue safety alone does not make close/drain/publication atomic.
